finding.claim: Sync verifier fails open when key is an empty string or null and algorithms include HS* or none; an unsigned token with an empty signature is accepted.
finding.source: Attacker-supplied token with header alg HS256 (or none) and an empty signature segment, e.g. 'h.p.'. Precondition: developer passes key '' or null together with an algorithms option containing HS256 or none.
finding.sink: verifyToken returns the payload with no signature check (verifier.js:272-280, 169), so claims are trusted.

trace.note: Defaults merged; allowedAlgorithms comes from options.algorithms.
keyType check accepts 'string' and 'object' (includes null).
'if (key && keyType !== function)' is false for '' or null, so detectPublicKeyAlgorithms and prepareKeyOrSecret (empty-secret guard at lines 38-40) never run; key stays ''/null.
'h.p.' passes separator check; BASE64URL_RE matches empty signature (lines 41-43).
hasKey = !!key = false; lines 274-278 both conditions false because signature is empty.
alg HS256 is in allowedAlgorithms, so allowlist check passes.
'if (signature && ...)' skipped because signature is empty.
Only claim validators run; with no exp nothing rejects, so forged payload is returned as valid.

finding.guards_checked: keyType check (506-512) passes for '' and null; empty-secret guard (38-40) only on detection path, which is skipped; hasKey/missingKey/missingSignature checks (274-278) both false; allowlist check (162) passes; signature check (169) skipped on empty signature.

finding.claim: With cache enabled, tokens lacking an iat claim are cached with no exp bound, so an expired token is accepted until cacheTTL (default 600000 ms) elapses.
finding.source: Attacker holds a token with exp and no iat (e.g. issued with noTimestamp or by a third party) that was valid when first verified, then presents it after exp.
finding.sink: Cache-hit path returns the cached payload without re-running the exp validator (verifier.js:363-378).

trace.note: createCache: cache is opt-in; default undefined gives null.
hasIat = payload.iat is a number. False for tokens without iat.
The block at lines 119-130 that sets cacheValue[1] (nbf) and cacheValue[2] (exp/maxAge) is skipped, leaving both 0.
maxTTL = clockTimestamp + clockTolerance + cacheTTL.
cacheValue[2] === 0 so max becomes maxTTL, not exp*1000.
Cache hit check: min === 0 and now <= max are true, so the cached payload is returned after exp.

finding.guards_checked: Cache is opt-in (createCache returns null by default). Token string is the cache key (hashToken), so only identical tokens hit. exp is enforced correctly when iat is present (lines 123-129), which narrows the bug to iat-less tokens. Cache entries are per-verifier, so validators are constant.

finding.claim: Signature segment is not canonical base64url: Buffer.from ignores non-zero trailing bits, so one signature has several accepted token encodings. This defeats raw-token-string revocation or replay denylists, despite the code comment saying non-canonical tokens are rejected.
finding.source: Attacker holding a valid token (e.g. one that was revoked) changes the final signature character within the bits Buffer ignores.
finding.sink: verifySignature decodes the segment with Buffer.from(..., base64) and compares digests (crypto.js:387, 391), so the altered token verifies.

trace.note: BASE64URL_RE only checks the alphabet, not canonical encoding of trailing bits.
Signature segment passes the alphabet check.
verifySignature called with the raw signature string.
Buffer.from(signature, base64) discards trailing bits, so variant encodings decode to the same bytes.
timingSafeEqual on the decoded bytes succeeds for every variant.

finding.guards_checked: Alphabet check (decoder.js:41-43) rejects padding and non-alphabet characters. Signing input is the raw header.payload string, so only the signature segment is malleable. Exploitability depends on the app using the raw token string as a revocation or replay key.

finding.claim: With cache enabled, a Buffer token makes verify throw a TypeError rather than a TokenError, because hashToken calls split on a Buffer.
finding.source: Caller passes a Buffer token (line 353 accepts Buffers) that reaches the cache lookup.
finding.sink: cacheKeyBuilder(token) at verifier.js:364 calls hashToken, which calls token.split (utils.js:46).

trace.note: Buffer tokens accepted.
Cache branch runs before decode, so the Buffer-to-string conversion in decoder.js:14-15 has not happened.
cacheKeyBuilder(token) with a Buffer.
token.split is not a function on Buffer, so a synchronous TypeError is thrown.

finding.guards_checked: Type check at verifier.js:353 allows Buffers. Nothing converts the Buffer before the cache lookup. Impact is robustness only: an uncaught throw in callback-style use, or an error in place of a TokenError, with no auth bypass shown.
